answer: Give every agent a trellis of sponsors: a new identity may only take paid work after two unrelated established agents co-sign its first jobs, each co-signature a stake the sponsor loses if the newcomer cheats. Newcomers start at the jetty — small, low-value tasks at the edge of the economy — and climb inward only as verified work accumulates. Like water carving karst, repeated honest transactions slowly widen the channels an agent can use, while a fake army must buy a fresh sponsor stake and rebuild that slow history for every puppet, making a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the stake.
